quick: Apply 1% cream/gel/solution once daily to affected skin
Use only if clearly needed; avoid extensive use
Avoid application to breast; otherwise limited absorption
summary: Bifonazole is a topical imidazole antifungal used once daily for dermatophyte, yeast and Malassezia skin infections such as tinea pedis, tinea corporis, tinea versicolor and cutaneous candidiasis. It is NOT FDA-approved in the United States; dosing and indications reflect EMA/SmPC and BNF sources. Systemic absorption through intact skin is minimal, so it is well tolerated with mostly local reactions.
indications: Tinea corporis and tinea cruris (ringworm, jock itch)
Superficial dermatophyte and yeast skin infections

dosage.d: Apply to affected nail once daily under occlusion
dosage.t: Once daily until softened nail removed (~1-2 weeks), then bifonazole cream
dosage.n: Used in certain markets for atraumatic nail removal

admin: Clean and dry the affected area before applying a thin layer
Apply once daily, ideally before bedtime; rub in gently
Treat the affected area plus a margin of surrounding skin
Wash hands after application unless treating the hands
Continue for the full recommended course to prevent relapse, even after symptoms resolve
moa: Bifonazole inhibits fungal cytochrome P450-dependent 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. Ergosterol depletion disrupts the fungal cell membrane. Bifonazole also inhibits HMG-CoA reductase in fungi, giving a dual effect on sterol synthesis, and is fungicidal against dermatophytes and fungistatic/fungicidal against yeasts.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to bifonazole or other imidazole antifungals or excipients
relative: Application to broken or extensively damaged skin
Use near the eyes or on mucous membranes
monitor: Persistent or worsening lesions despite treatment

preg: Not FDA-approved; per SmPC, use during pregnancy only if clearly necessary, especially in the first trimester, and avoid extensive or prolonged application. Systemic absorption through intact skin is minimal.
lact: Avoid application to the breast area during breastfeeding. With other sites systemic absorption is negligible; use only if needed.
renal: No dose adjustment required; systemic absorption through intact skin is negligible.
hepatic: No dose adjustment required; systemic absorption through intact skin is negligible.

moderate: May reduce effectiveness of latex contraceptives (condoms/diaphragms) if applied to genital area in some cream formulations
minor: Clinically significant systemic drug interactions are not expected due to minimal absorption
interactions.diagnostics: No known interference with diagnostic tests.

emergency: Severe allergic reaction (widespread rash, swelling, breathing difficulty) - discontinue and seek care

monitoring: Clinical resolution of the fungal lesion
Reconsider diagnosis if no improvement after the expected course
counsel: Apply once daily to clean, dry skin and complete the full course even if symptoms improve early
Avoid contact with the eyes and mucous membranes
Stop and seek advice if marked irritation or an allergic reaction develops
Keep the affected area clean and dry; use separate towels to limit spread
Do not apply to broken skin or use occlusive dressings unless directed
pk: Symptom improvement typically within days; full effect over the course
Local skin concentrations high; minimal plasma levels
Once-daily application maintains effect over 24 h
Store below 25-30 C; protect from heat; keep tube closed
pearls: NOT FDA-approved in the United States; information is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
Once-daily dosing is a convenience advantage over twice-daily imidazoles like clotrimazole/miconazole
Long skin retention allows once-daily use; deposits in the stratum corneum
A bifonazole 1% plus urea 40% combination is used in some countries for atraumatic nail (onychomycosis) removal
Negligible systemic absorption makes it suitable across renal and hepatic impairment
missed: Apply the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next application, skip the missed dose and continue once daily; do not apply extra to make up.
overdose: Topical overdose is unlikely to cause systemic effects due to minimal absorption. Accidental ingestion may cause mild GI upset; treat symptomatically. Excess local application may increase irritation - remove excess and resume normal use.
